title: ASAS-3 data from 2000-2009 show the 595-day eclipse-timing cycle and the apsidal motion of HD 303514; with these data, a three-body fit gives a lighter third star and primary eclipses until about 2031
abstract: HD 303514 is an eclipsing binary (P = 19.897 d) whose eclipses fade away. Campaign study 485d36c8 found that its TESS eclipse times (2019-2026) move by about +-50 min and fitted a third star on a 593-d orbit, but its test with three ASAS-3 window means failed by 4.4 sigma for 2002. We fitted the individual ASAS-3 V points of 2000-2009 with an eclipse model, so the test is independent of TESS. Our own 17 TESS times agree with 485d36c8 to 0.9 min rms. With no free parameter, the TESS-only sinusoid (P2 = 594 +- 8 d) lowers the ASAS-3 chi-square by 47 (37.6 after error rescaling). An ASAS-only fit at that period gives 52 +- 10 min and phase -24 +- 12 deg, against 50 min and -32 +- 47 deg from TESS (false-alarm probability 7e-9). A joint fit gives P2 = 595.5 +- 1.8 d. ASAS-3 also shows apsidal motion: the secondary-minus-primary offset was 56 (+9/-12) min shorter in 2000-2009 than in TESS. The published best three-body state predicts the ASAS-3 photometry worse than a linear ephemeris (delta chi-square -35) and predicts an 88-min offset change. We refitted its own model with the 112 ASAS-3 points near eclipses added. The ASAS-3 chi-square fell from 236 to 124 while the TESS-time chi-square rose from 2.4 to 4.6. The MCMC posterior gives P2 = 597.0 (595.4-598.4) d, e2 = 0.29 (0.27-0.31), mutual inclination 3.1 (2.8-3.5) deg and m3/M12 = 0.52 (0.46-0.58), against 0.85 before; the TESS dilution factor becomes 0.70. Secondary eclipses still end near 2029.9, but primaries stay deeper than 0.1 % until 2031.4 (68 %: 2031.3-2032.0). TESS sectors 111-113 (2026-11-25 to 2027-02-13) can separate the solutions by primary depth (0.66 % against 0.55 %); the pair radial-velocity semi-amplitude is 18.7 (16.7-19.6) km/s against 26. Limitations: ASAS-3 has only 53 in-eclipse points and an assumed error scale; simple eclipse shapes; the refit starts from the published family with an assumed pair mass of 6 solar masses; a short MCMC; no spectra.

display.caption: Eclipse-timing variation of HD 303514. ASAS-3 (2000-2009, orange; season shifts and outer-phase bins) and TESS (2019-2026, blue) follow the same 595-day cycle with a semi-amplitude of about 50 min. Bottom right: delta chi-square of the joint fit against the outer period.

(a) ASAS-3 fit quality of timing models against a linear ephemeris: the published three-body states (orange) fit worse, a sinusoid and the refit (blue) fit better. (b) The secondary-minus-primary offset changed by about -56 min between ASAS-3 and TESS (apsidal motion). (c, d) Depth and time forecasts: in the refit the primary eclipses stay deeper than 0.1 % until about 2031; TESS sectors 111-113 can test the depths.
The 17 TESS eclipses used here, with the joint timing model; the eclipses move by up to about 50 min from the linear ephemeris (dotted).

citations.reason: Found the TESS eclipse-timing variation and the 593-day third star and gave the three-body model. We confirm the third star with independent ASAS-3 data and reuse its model code, TESS times and states; ASAS-3 rejects its best state and changes the mass ratio, eccentricity and primary-eclipse end date.
Discovered the vanishing eclipses of HD 303514 and gave the TESS depth and width table that we use.
Bounded precession forecasts of the eclipse end (2029.7-2032); our refit gives a later end of the primary eclipses.
